gloss: much the same; six of one, half a dozen of the other

definitions.gloss: much the same; about the same; six of one, half a dozen of the other
definitions.explanation: Used when two or more things are so similar that there is no meaningful difference between them. Often implies that none of the options is particularly good.

examples.japanese: どちらも{似|に}たり{寄|よ}ったりだ。
{値段|ねだん}はどの{店|みせ}も{似|に}たり{寄|よ}ったりだった。
examples.english: The prices were about the same at every store.

examples.japanese: {候補者|こうほしゃ}の{主張|しゅちょう}はどれも{似|に}たり{寄|よ}ったりで、{違|ちが}いがわからなかった。
examples.english: The candidates' positions were all much the same, and I couldn't tell the difference.

notes:
Combines {似|に}たり (being similar) and {寄|よ}ったり (being close), reinforcing the idea of near-identical similarity. The たり form of both verbs creates a rhythmic, set expression.

USAGE:
Often carries a slightly dismissive or negative nuance — implying that none of the options stands out or that they are all equally mediocre. Used as a predicate with だ or as a modifier with の.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- どれも{似|に}たり{寄|よ}ったり — they're all much the same
- {似|に}たり{寄|よ}ったりの{結果|けっか} — similar results
- {似|に}たり{寄|よ}ったりの{内容|ないよう} — similar content

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {大同小異|だいどうしょうい} — much the same with minor differences (more formal, literary)
- {五十歩百歩|ごじっぽひゃっぽ} — pot calling the kettle black; equally bad (stronger negative nuance)
- {同|おな}じようなもの — about the same thing (plain, neutral)
